original_question: With the same definitions of Ufin and Sfin for cover classes, if Ufin(O,Omega) is not equal to Sfin(Gamma,Omega), does Ufin(O,Gamma) imply Sfin(Gamma,Omega)?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 2.1(2): "And if not, does Ufin(O, Γ) imply Sfin(Γ, Ω)?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly isolates the second clause of Problem 2.1 in the paper, including the conditional dependence on a negative answer to Problem 2.1(1), and it uses the same three cover classes O, Ω, Γ and the same two selection principles Ufin and Sfin that appear in the paper’s formulation.
missing_details: The paper’s scope here is sets of real numbers; the question should quantify over a set of reals X rather than speak only at the level of abstract cover classes.
O should be defined as the collection of nontrivial open covers of X.
Ω should be defined as the collection of open ω-covers of X: X is not itself a member of the cover, and every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some member of the cover.
Γ should be defined as the collection of open γ-covers of X: the cover is infinite, and each x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of the cover.
Sfin(A,B) should be stated explicitly: for every sequence (Un)n in A, there are finite Fn ⊆ Un such that ⋃n Fn is a member of B.
Ufin(A,B) should be stated explicitly: for every sequence (Un)n in A with no finite subcover, there are finite Fn ⊆ Un such that {⋃Fn : n ∈ N} is a member of B.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should ask whether every X satisfying Ufin(O,Γ) must also satisfy Sfin(Γ,Ω), under the assumption Ufin(O,Ω) ≠ Sfin(Γ,Ω).
The paper places this as one of the only two unsettled implications in the Scheepers diagram; that contextual restriction is implicit in the draft.
Because the paper is about sets of reals, it later notes that open covers may be assumed countable; this is implicit rather than stated in the draft.
refined_question: In the setting of sets of real numbers, let X be a set of reals, let O be the family of all nontrivial open covers of X, let Ω be the family of open ω-covers of X, and let Γ be the family of open γ-covers of X. For cover classes A and B, define Sfin(A,B) to mean that for every sequence (Un)n∈N of members of A there exist finite sets Fn ⊆ Un such that ⋃n∈N Fn is a member of B; define Ufin(A,B) to mean that for every sequence (Un)n∈N of members of A having no finite subcover, there exist finite sets Fn ⊆ Un such that {⋃Fn : n ∈ N} is a member of B. Assuming that Ufin(O,Ω) is not equal to Sfin(Γ,Ω), must every set of reals X satisfying Ufin(O,Γ) also satisfy Sfin(Γ,Ω)?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 2, Problem 2.1(2), not a broader neighboring question. In the paper’s Scheepers-diagram discussion, Tsaban states that almost all non-diagram implications are already known to be unprovable under CH, and that only two implications remain unsettled; he then lists Problem 2.1, whose second clause matches your draft verbatim up to missing scope/notation details. The needed notation is introduced in Section 1: Sfin(A,B), Ufin(A,B), O, Ω, and Γ are all defined there, with covers understood to be nontrivial open covers, and the chapter explicitly says that all problems discussed are about sets of real numbers. I therefore kept the question narrowly on Problem 2.1(2), made the ambient object X explicit, and spelled out the definitions so the result is stand-alone. I did not add an alternate formulation, because the paper only says that Problem 2.1 can be reformulated in terms of sets generating Borel non-σ-compact groups and that Problem 2.3 would imply Problem 2.1(2); it does not itself state an explicit equivalent formulation in full detail.
